account:
Today I have heard repeated, vague reports of a bridge or port change associated with the bakery. One townsman said the baker and my dockside neighbour were there, and that the baker carried a sack of bread. I have not witnessed a meeting or any change myself. The repetition may be gossip rather than independent corroboration. The builder reports no confirmed damage, so I have no basis for assuming repairs are involved. Bread deliveries or other transport arrangements seem possible, but their purpose remains unknown. I should ask the neighbour at our fifteen hundred tea rather than treat a rumour as fact.

Town business has been frustratingly poorly documented. This morning's scheduled mill grain inspection named no host or operator, and no reserve stocks were shown. That is an incomplete inspection, not evidence of a shortage. I funded the secretary to obtain stationery and requested a draft council letter seeking the operator's identity, reserve-stock location and a hosted inspection. She says no urgent correspondence has arrived. Two books in the appointments chest are accounts-review and treasury records; she had not identified the third. I saw her return a book to the chest, but do not know its contents. My last question about the bakery news went unheard because she had left. Nothing yet establishes wrongdoing or an organized effort to exclude me, though I still want to understand the bakery reports.
